entities.summary:
Quintus Dellius was a Roman commander and politician who played a significant role in the late 1st century BC.


 As a member of the equestrian class, Dellius held various positions, including that of legate and governor of the Roman province of Asia Minor.


 His most notable achievement was his leadership of the Roman forces during the Mithridatic Wars, a series of conflicts with the Kingdom of Pontus in modern-day Turkey.


 Dellius's military successes helped secure Roman control over the region and cemented his reputation as a skilled and ambitious commander.


 Despite his importance, Dellius's life was cut short in 100 BCE, leaving behind a legacy as a notable figure in Roman history.


 Quintus Dellius's story serves as a fascinating case study of the complexities of Roman politics and the pivotal role of military leaders in shaping the course of empire.
